note: REQUIRED axis-9 edge (P/anticipatory-application). Kreijns et al. are this cluster's clearest skeptical-pole source, positioned against ped-sec-25 (Gunawardena & Zittle) and ped-sec-28 (Richardson & Swan)'s affirmative predictor-of-satisfaction findings. Precise stance: the article does not deny social presence has effects; true to its own title, it argues social interaction (and the social presence that depends on it) is systematically ASSUMED to occur automatically once technology permits it, and rarely deliberately scaffolded -- so predictor-style findings elsewhere in the literature describe environments that happen to have solved a design problem this review diagnoses as usually unsolved.
